record.paper_title: Known Results and Open Problems on C1 linearization in Banach Spaces
record.original_question: Suppose the nonlinear part in a local map T(x)=Ax+X(x) on an infinite-dimensional Banach space vanishes to order higher than two near the fixed point, for example X(x)=O(|x|^{1+η}) with η>0 instead of merely X(x)=O(|x|^2). Do such higher-order nonlinearities permit weaker spectral restrictions on the linear part A than the non-resonance condition (2) required in the C^1 linearization theorem stated as Theorem 3?

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Higher order nonlinearities. As it is seen in the statement of Theorem 3 it is considered that the nonlinearity X(x) vanishes together with its first derivative at x = 0. Since the nonlinearity is of class C1,1 this amounts to say that X(x) = O(|x|2). As it happens in Theorem 2 one can expect that larger values of η if X(x) = O(|x|1+η) would give less restrictive conditions on σ(A) in (2). This deserves to be studied.

Observe that η is restricted to be positive, but otherwise can be large. It is easy to see that the inequality ||A−1|| ||A||1+η < 1 is satisfied by an equivalent norm ... if and only if |σ(A)| is contained in an open interval of the form (a−, a+) with (a+)1+η < a−. So, the restrictions on σ(A) become weaker when the order of the nonlinearity near zero becomes larger. This will give rise to one of the open problems below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be an infinite-dimensional Banach space and let $A\colon E	o E$ be a bounded invertible linear operator. Consider a local map $T\colon U	o E$ defined on a neighborhood $U$ of $0$ by
$$T(x)=Ax+X(x),$$
where $X$ is of class $C^{1,1}$ with $X(0)=0$, $DX(0)=0$, and in fact satisfies the higher-order vanishing condition
$$\|X(x)\|=O(\|x\|^{1+\eta}),\qquad \|DX(x)-DX(y)\|=O(\max(\|x\|,\|y\|)^{\eta-1}\|x-y\|)$$
for some constant $\eta>0$ (so the standard quadratic case corresponds to $\eta=1$).

Recall that a known $C^1$ linearization theorem in this setting asserts that if the spectrum $\sigma(A)$ satisfies the non-resonance / band condition
$$\|A^{-1}\|\cdot \|A\|^{2}<1\qquad\text{(in some equivalent norm),}$$
equivalently $\sigma(A)\subset\{z:a_-<|z|<a_+\}$ with $a_+^{2}<a_-$, then $T$ is locally $C^1$-conjugate near $0$ to its linear part $A$.

Note that for general $\eta>0$ the condition $\|A^{-1}\|\cdot\|A\|^{1+\eta}<1$ in some equivalent norm is equivalent to $\sigma(A)$ being contained in an open annulus $\{a_-<|z|<a_+\}$ with $a_+^{1+\eta}<a_-$, which is strictly weaker than the case $\eta=1$ when $\eta>1$.

Problem. Determine whether, for $\eta>1$, higher-order vanishing of the nonlinearity $X(x)=O(\|x\|^{1+\eta})$ permits a correspondingly weaker spectral restriction on $A$ — namely the band condition $a_+^{1+\eta}<a_-$ in place of $a_+^{2}<a_-$ — under which $T$ is still locally $C^1$-conjugate to $A$ near $0$. More precisely, prove or disprove: for every bounded invertible $A$ on $E$ with $\sigma(A)$ contained in an annulus satisfying $a_+^{1+\eta}<a_-$, and every $C^{1,1}$ nonlinearity $X$ with $\|X(x)\|=O(\|x\|^{1+\eta})$, there exists a local $C^1$ diffeomorphism $h$ fixing $0$ with $h\circ T = A\circ h$ near $0$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not locate a paper establishing the conjectured weaker spectral band condition $a_+^{1+\eta}<a_-$ for $C^1$ linearization in infinite-dimensional Banach spaces under higher-order nonlinearities $X(x)=O(\|x\|^{1+\eta})$. Related works (e.g., on sharp regularity of linearization for $C^{1,1}$ hyperbolic diffeomorphisms and on $C^1$ linearization in Banach spaces under gap and band conditions) treat the case $\eta=1$ or related regularity refinements but do not appear to resolve the higher-$\eta$ question. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: C^1 linearization for C^{1,1} hyperbolic diffeomorphisms under gap and band conditions on the spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Existing C^1 linearization results in Banach spaces treat the standard quadratic nonlinearity case and a band condition tied to it; the higher-order analog is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: C^1 invariant, stable and inertial manifolds for non-autonomous dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on C^1 invariant manifolds and linearization does not address the precise question of weaker spectral restrictions under higher-order nonlinearity vanishing.
status_evidence.claim: No located source resolves the question of whether higher-order vanishing yields a weaker non-resonance band condition for C^1 linearization in Banach spaces.
